conventions: An article on הָאֱלֹהִים standing in apposition to the rectum יְהוָה of a construct chain (בֵּית יְהוָה הָאֱלֹהִים 22.1, מִקְדַּשׁ יְהוָה הָאֱלֹהִים 22.19) is not the rectum's article and does not take the phrase's fronted the under rule 29: the ASV writes God bare, so the article is unrepresented and the construct noun takes a supplied the. Where the article stands on the rectum itself (בֵּית הָאֱלֹהִים 22.2, כְלֵי קֹדֶשׁ הָאֱלֹהִים 22.19) rule 29's fronting case governs and the article takes the the while the construct is bare.

מִסָּבִיב is one fused unit with the מִן under rule 40's absolute-noun adverb clause wherever the ASV writes a single adverbial rendering for the pair — round about (22.9, headed on round) and on every side (22.18, headed on side); the preposition is not marked unrepresented beside the adverb.
report: Read all 19 verses end to end against the 38-lemma candidate table. Every multi-treatment bucket is licensed by the ASV's own wording: לְ takes to/for/of/unto/after/into/that where the ASV writes those words and is unrepresented where a dative or object-marking lə is recast bare (22.9, 22.12, 22.17, 22.18) or where a coordinated lə-phrase is rendered under one written of (22.14, 22.16); לָרֹב is split into in + abundance in 22.3, 22.4, 22.14, 22.15 and fused as abundantly in 22.5 and 22.8, exactly as rule 40 directs; מִסָּבִיב is fused with its מִן in both 22.9 (round about) and 22.18 (on every side); לִפְנֵי fuses in 22.5 and 22.18; אַיִן takes without (22.3, 22.14) or there is no (22.16) as written.

The one construction that could have split — the article on הָאֱלֹהִים inside a construct chain — is consistent: where the article stands on the rectum itself (בֵּית הָאֱלֹהִים 22.2, כְלֵי קֹדֶשׁ הָאֱלֹהִים 22.19) it takes the phrase's fronted the and the construct is bare; where it stands on an appositive to the rectum יְהוָה (בֵּית יְהוָה הָאֱלֹהִים 22.1, מִקְדַּשׁ יְהוָה הָאֱלֹהִים 22.19) the ASV writes God bare, the article is unrepresented, and the construct takes a supplied the. Recorded as a convention.

BSB disagreements are all convention differences, none an error: the resumptive הוּא of 22.1 sends its copula to the predicate under rule 20; the three unrepresented articles are on God written bare (22.1, 22.19) and all countries (22.5); the nine R and four Rd lə's are datives recast bare, the lə of לֵאמֹר, and coordinated lə-phrases the ASV renders under one of. No accepted edge changed.

The large-source-unit candidate in 22.5 (לְמַעְלָה → exceeding, three morphemes) is a preposition, adverb and directive he rendered by one English word and is genuinely indivisible under rules 30 and 32.

Single-occurrence judgments that carry a named alternative in their notes and were left standing: הַצֹּרִים → they of Tyre with they on the article (22.4), לְאֵין → without fused (22.4), נָא → therefore (22.5), וְלִשְׁמוֹר → that so with so on the waw (22.12). None recurs in the chapter, so none is a split.
No promotion: the chapter teaches nothing the contract does not already say, and the appositive-article judgment lacks corpus precedent in the briefing.
